questions.q: In the example, 1,840 cases opened and 1,725 closed this month. What happened to the open backlog?
options: It shrank by 115
It stayed the same
It grew by 115
It doubled
questions.explain: Opened minus closed is 115, so the backlog grew by that many cases over the month.

questions.q: Your workload chart has a bar labeled 'Tier 1' much larger than the agents' bars. What is it most likely?
options: A single overloaded agent named Tier
A queue: cases waiting in a queue show the queue as the case owner
A duplicate of the total backlog
An error in the Cases report type
questions.explain: Cases assigned to a queue have the queue as owner. Note this in the chart title so viewers don't read it as one person's workload.

questions.q: What is the purpose of bucketing the Age field into ranges like 0-2, 3-5, and 6+ days on the aging report?
options: It deletes old cases
It sorts rows into readable age bands so the reader can see and act on the oldest cases
It changes the priority of each case
It is required for dashboards to load
questions.explain: Bucketing groups a numeric field into named bands, making the aging table easier to scan and act on.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a daily backlog trend needs historical trend reporting or reporting snapshots?
options: Standard reports show current records, so past daily backlog values must be captured over time to be reported
Dashboards cannot display more than one number
Backlog cannot be counted at all
Cases have no status field
questions.explain: A standard report reflects records as they are now. Trend reporting needs history captured by trend features or scheduled snapshots, set up in advance.

questions.q: With 412 open cases spread over 12 agents, what is the approximate average load, and why is it useful?
options: About 12 per agent, a target set by Salesforce
About 412 per agent, since all agents share cases
About 3 per agent, matching the priority count
About 34 per agent, a sanity check for the workload bars
questions.explain: 412 divided by 12 is about 34. If the bars on the workload chart average far from that, something in the report filters or grouping is off.
